protocol_overview.type: Industrial Ethernet fieldbus with on-the-fly frame processing. The MainDevice (Master) circulates Ethernet frames carrying one or more EtherCAT datagrams; SubDevices (Slaves) implemented as EtherCAT Slave Controllers (ESC) read/modify/forward the frame while it is passing through their MAC. Layered above the wire: 13-command addressing scheme, 6-state EtherCAT State Machine (ESM), SyncManager + FMMU memory model, optional Distributed Clocks for nanosecond synchronization, and mailbox-resident application protocols (CoE / SoE / EoE / FoE / AoE).
protocol_overview.transport: Standard 100BASE-TX (100 Mb/s) or 100BASE-FX Ethernet for the base spec; EtherCAT G extends to 1 Gb/s. Two carrier modes: (a) raw Ethernet frames with EtherType 0x88A4 (default, low-latency on-segment), (b) UDP/IP encapsulation on port 0x88A4 (cross-network routing through standard IP infrastructure). Each Ethernet frame carries a 16-bit EtherCAT header (11-bit length + 1-bit reserved + 4-bit type=0x1 for ESC datagrams) followed by one or more datagrams.
protocol_overview.duplex: Full duplex (100BASE-TX always full duplex; CSMA/CD is never used; PHY auto-negotiation locks to 100 Mb/s full duplex).
protocol_overview.topology_supported: Line (daisy-chain — dominant), tree, star, ring with redundancy, drop line, mixed; up to 65,535 SubDevices per logical bus.
protocol_overview.master_count: Single MainDevice per logical bus in the cyclic phase. EAP (EtherCAT Automation Protocol) enables MainDevice-to-MainDevice exchange at the plant level.
protocol_overview.synchronization: Distributed Clocks (DC) sub-protocol: the first DC-capable SubDevice acts as Reference Clock; the MainDevice uses ARMW (Cmd 0x0D) datagrams to propagate that clock to every other DC-capable SubDevice. Hardware offset + drift compensation yields <100 ns jitter across the network.
interfaces_in_scope: ESC IO (two or more Fast/Gigabit Ethernet ports, with on-the-fly forwarding logic)
PDI (Process Data Interface) on the application side of the ESC: asynchronous µC bus, synchronous µC bus, SPI, Digital I/O, on-chip CPU bus
EEPROM SII interface (I²C-compatible 2-wire) carrying the ESI descriptor
MainDevice = standard Ethernet NIC; no EtherCAT-specific hardware required

functional_requirements.text: Every EtherCAT frame on the wire shall be a standard Ethernet frame (Preamble + SFD + DA + SA + EtherType + Payload + FCS) with EtherType = 0x88A4 (Raw-Ethernet mode) or shall be encapsulated inside a UDP/IP packet with destination UDP port 0x88A4 (UDP/IP mode). The Destination MAC on raw-Ethernet frames is unconstrained (any unicast / multicast) because SubDevices forward irrespective of DA.

The EtherCAT header is exactly 16 bits: Length[10:0] = total length in bytes of the following datagrams excluding this header, Reserved[12] = 0, Type[15:12] = 0x1 for ESC datagrams (Type 0x4 is reserved for the Network Variable protocol of EAP).

Each EtherCAT datagram begins with a 10-byte header: Cmd[7:0] (command, see FR-CMD-04), Idx[7:0] (datagram index — MainDevice-local opaque identifier returned unchanged by SubDevices), Address[31:0] (interpretation depends on Cmd — split into Position/ADP/Logical), Length[10:0] (datagram data length 1-1486 in bytes), Reserved[2:0]=0, Circulating[14] (set if the datagram has already gone around the network once), Next[15] (set if another datagram follows after this one's data + WKC), IRQ[15:0] (logical OR of AL Status interrupt requests, set by SubDevices). The datagram ends with the data field (Length bytes) and a 16-bit Working Counter (WKC).

The Cmd field takes one of 15 values: 0x00 NOP, 0x01 APRD (Auto-Increment Read), 0x02 APWR (Auto-Increment Write), 0x03 APRW (Auto-Increment ReadWrite), 0x04 FPRD (Fixed Physical Read), 0x05 FPWR (Fixed Physical Write), 0x06 FPRW (Fixed Physical ReadWrite), 0x07 BRD (Broadcast Read), 0x08 BWR (Broadcast Write), 0x09 BRW (Broadcast ReadWrite), 0x0A LRD (Logical Read), 0x0B LWR (Logical Write), 0x0C LRW (Logical ReadWrite), 0x0D ARMW (Auto-Increment Read, Multiple Write), 0x0E FRMW (Fixed Read, Multiple Write). All other Cmd values are reserved and shall be ignored.

Auto-Increment addressing (APRD / APWR / APRW / ARMW): the Address field's high half is interpreted as a signed Position (16-bit two's complement) that is incremented by every SubDevice as the frame passes through. A SubDevice executes the access when its incremented Position becomes 0x0000. This is used during start-up before SubDevices have been assigned a Configured Station Address.

Fixed Physical addressing (FPRD / FPWR / FPRW / FRMW): the Address field's high half is the 16-bit Configured Station Address (ESC register 0x0010-0x0011, set by the MainDevice during start-up). A SubDevice executes the access when its Configured Station Address equals the datagram's address.

Broadcast addressing (BRD / BWR / BRW): the Address field's high half is ignored; every SubDevice executes the access. The low 16 bits give the local ESC offset. BRD / BWR / BRW are used for status sweeps, broadcast state transitions, and any operation that targets all SubDevices uniformly.

Logical addressing (LRD / LWR / LRW): the Address field is the full 32-bit Logical Address of the network-wide 4 GByte logical-address space; every SubDevice's FMMUs map a region of this logical space onto a region of the SubDevice's local ESC memory. Multiple SubDevices can contribute to or read from the same LRD/LWR datagram simultaneously. This is the principal mechanism for cyclic process-data exchange.

Every datagram has a 16-bit Working Counter (WKC) appended after the data field. SubDevices increment WKC by +1 on successful read, +2 on successful write, +3 on successful read-write. The MainDevice compares the returned WKC against an expected total. Datagrams that fail to reach all expected SubDevices return a smaller WKC, signalling a missing or misconfigured SubDevice.

Distributed Clocks (DC): the first DC-capable SubDevice's ESC time (ESC register 0x0900-0x0907) is the System Time reference. The MainDevice issues an ARMW (Cmd 0x0D) datagram with the reference SubDevice's local time, which every downstream DC-capable SubDevice reads and writes into its own System Time Offset (0x0920-0x0927); the SubDevices then continuously close the loop between local PHY-derived time and System Time, achieving <100 ns jitter.

FMMU (Fieldbus Memory Management Unit): up to 8 per SubDevice, registers 0x0600-0x06FF. Each FMMU entry specifies (Logical Start Address (32b), Length (16b), Logical Start Bit (3b), Logical Stop Bit (3b), Physical Start Address (16b), Physical Start Bit (3b), Type[1] = Read, Type[2] = Write, Active[7:0]) and maps a contiguous slice of network-wide Logical Address space onto a contiguous slice of local ESC memory at bit granularity. FMMUs are written by the MainDevice during the transition Init → PreOp.

SyncManager (SM): up to 8 channels per SubDevice, registers 0x0800-0x08FF. Each SM is configured as either (a) Mailbox mode = handshake atomic write-then-read with retry/timeout, or (b) Buffered (process-data) mode = 1 / 2 / 3-buffer ring with hardware overrun protection. SM0 + SM1 are the canonical mailbox pair (MBox-Out + MBox-In); SM2 + SM3 are the canonical process-data pair (Outputs + Inputs).

EtherCAT State Machine (ESM) has six states: Init (initial after power-up), PreOp (Pre-Operational — mailbox communication only), SafeOp (Safe-Operational — inputs valid, outputs in Safe state), Op (Operational — full cyclic process-data exchange), Boot (firmware update), and the implicit Off state. The MainDevice requests the next state via AL Control (0x0120); the SubDevice confirms via AL Status (0x0130); errors are reported in AL Status Code (0x0134). The legal transitions are Init↔PreOp, PreOp↔SafeOp, SafeOp↔Op, and Init↔Boot.

Each SubDevice contains an EtherCAT Slave Controller (ESC) with at least: 64 KByte register+DPRAM space at 0x0000-0xFFFF; 2-4 Fast or Gigabit Ethernet ports with on-the-fly processing engine, port loop-back, auto-forwarding, and per-port CRC error counters; SII (EEPROM) state machine; FMMU array (typically 8); SyncManager array (typically 8); Distributed Clock unit (optional); ESM hardware support (AL Event mask + INT output).

Each ESC exposes one Process Data Interface (PDI) to the application-side microcontroller. The choice of PDI (asynchronous µC bus / synchronous µC bus / SPI / Digital I/O / on-chip CPU bus) is configured in the SII EEPROM at SII offset 0x0140 (PDI Control). The PDI gives the local µC byte-level read/write access to the entire 64-KByte ESC memory.

Each SubDevice has an external serial EEPROM (1 Kbit to 4 Mbit, I²C-compatible 2-wire) holding the EtherCAT Slave Information (ESI) descriptor: Vendor ID, Product Code, Revision Number, Serial Number, Default SyncManager + FMMU configuration, Mailbox SM configuration, Bootstrap configuration, supported Mailbox Protocols bitmask (CoE / SoE / EoE / FoE / AoE / VoE bits), and PDI configuration. The ESC reads SII at power-up and re-reads on demand.

CoE (CANopen over EtherCAT) — re-uses the entire CiA 301 / CiA 4xx Object Dictionary model. CoE messages are carried in the mailbox: SDO Read / SDO Write / SDO Information / PDO. The Object Dictionary is indexed by 16-bit Index + 8-bit Subindex. DS-402 drive profile is the canonical Op-state command structure for motion-control SubDevices.
SoE (Sercos over EtherCAT) — wraps the IEC 61800-7 / Sercos III IDN-addressed parameter access protocol inside the mailbox; primarily for servo drive integration in Sercos-historic installations.

EoE (Ethernet over EtherCAT) — tunnels arbitrary 802.3 Ethernet frames inside EtherCAT mailbox messages; allows IP applications (HTTP, FTP, etc.) on a SubDevice to reach the outside world via the MainDevice's standard NIC.
FoE (File access over EtherCAT) — TFTP-like simple file transfer for firmware update; typically used in Boot state. Provides WRQ / RRQ / DATA / ACK / ERROR packets.
AoE (ADS over EtherCAT) — routed messaging (AMS Net Id + Port) layered on the mailbox; used by Beckhoff TwinCAT and similar runtimes for symbolic variable access and remote procedure call.

Safety over EtherCAT (FSoE, IEC 61784-3-12) — black-channel-principle safety frame layered on the mailbox; SIL 3 / Cat 4 / PL e capable. The underlying EtherCAT network is NOT safety-rated; only the FSoE end-points are.

Each ESC port (Port 0 / Port 1 / Port 2 / Port 3) has hardware-implemented automatic loopback: if no active link partner is present on a downstream port the ESC closes the loop internally and forwards the frame back upstream; this is what makes daisy-chain + auto-return work without explicit configuration.

The forwarding latency through one ESC is typically ~1 µs at 100 Mb/s (ranging by ESC vendor: 300 ns - 1.5 µs). The propagation-delay measurement registers (0x0900-0x09FF) let the MainDevice characterise the actual delay through every SubDevice for DC compensation.

Hot Connect / Hot Swap defines groups of SubDevices that may join / leave the network during operation. The MainDevice tolerates the absence of any Hot Connect group (the corresponding LRD/LWR datagrams' WKC will be lower than the maximum but the cyclic exchange continues for the remaining SubDevices).

error_response_conditions.text: FCS error on receive (per-port hardware-counted in ESC registers 0x0300-0x030F): forwarded frames continue, the FCS error counter increments, RX_ER is asserted on the PDI as a notification.

Working Counter mismatch (MainDevice-detected): the MainDevice compares the returned WKC of each datagram against the expected count; mismatch is escalated to the application layer as a per-datagram WKC error.

AL Status mismatch (ESC register 0x0130): if the SubDevice cannot satisfy a MainDevice-requested ESM transition, AL Status holds the previous state OR'ed with the Error bit (bit 4), and AL Status Code (0x0134) carries the IEC 61158-defined error number.

PDI watchdog (ESC register 0x0410-0x041F): if no PDI write to the configured watchdog trigger location arrives within the configured timeout, the watchdog expires, asserts PDI WD pin, optionally resets process-data outputs to Safe state.
SyncManager error (ESC register 0x0805 SM Status): mailbox-mode SM reports buffer-full / buffer-empty; buffered-mode SM reports buffer-overrun; lost-mailbox is reported by a unique SM watchdog.

Link loss on any port (ESC register 0x0110 DL Status): the affected port's Loop-State changes from open to closed; the ESC automatically forwards traffic on the loop-back path; the MainDevice observes the topology change in subsequent diagnostic reads.

compliance_requirements: EtherCAT Conformance Test (ETG.1500 / ETG.1500.1) — mandatory before commercial release of any EtherCAT SubDevice; verifies frame-level behavior, ESM transitions, mailbox protocols, FMMU/SM correctness, DC compatibility.
EtherCAT MainDevice Classification (ETG.1500.2): Class A (full feature set) vs Class B (basic feature set) compliance categories.
Vendor ID assignment by the ETG (32-bit IEEE-style identifier); 16-bit prefix uniquely identifies the vendor in CoE/SoE Object Dictionary entries.
ESI (EtherCAT Slave Information) XML file published by the SubDevice vendor; XML schema defined by ETG.2000.
Safety over EtherCAT (FSoE) certification per IEC 61784-3-12 for SIL 3 / Cat 4 / PL e SubDevices.
IEC 61158 Type 12 + IEC 61784 CPF 12 international standardization; SEMI E54.20 standardization for semiconductor equipment.
